result:
**The proposed answer of 64 is not supported by the argument given, and I believe the true minimum is smaller.**

The solution asserts that isomorphic conjugacy quandles force isoclinism for all orders below 64, but it gives no argument or citation for this. Isoclinism is the natural candidate invariant here, since isoclinic groups have isomorphic commutator structure, but a quandle isomorphism of conjugacy quandles need not respect the full isoclinism data. I recall work on conjugacy quandles and isoclinism (Bonatto and coauthors) that exhibits non-isoclinic groups with isomorphic conjugacy quandles at orders well below 64, and I believe the smallest such pair occurs at order 32. I cannot verify this from memory with certainty, and I did not run a computer search (for example, with GAP's SmallGroups library and a quandle isomorphism test), so I cannot state the exact minimum.

What I can say is that the proposed answer rests on an unjustified claim, and I have reason to think it is wrong.

VERDICT: REJECT
